name: Squash Messy Commits
problem: You've been working on a feature and made 10 tiny, messy commits (like 'fix typo', 'update css', 'oops fixed css again'). You want to combine them into one clean commit before opening a pull request.

steps.title: Start an interactive rebase
steps.description: Tell Git you want to interactively rebase the last 10 commits. This opens your configured text editor.

steps.title: Change 'pick' to 'squash'
steps.description: In the editor, you'll see a list of your commits from oldest to newest. Leave the top one as `pick`. Change the word `pick` to `squash` (or just `s`) for all the others.
steps.code:
pick a1b2c3d Add login form structure
squash e4f5g6h Add CSS styling
squash i7j8k9l Fix typo in button
squash m1n2o3p Fix CSS alignment

# Save and close the editor.

steps.title: Write the final commit message
steps.description: Git will open the editor again, combining all the commit messages into one file. Delete the messy ones and write a single, clean description.
steps.code:
# Delete the old lines and write:
Add login form with validation

- Implemented HTML structure
- Added responsive CSS styling
- Included client-side validation logic

# Save and close.

steps.title: Force push (if previously pushed)
steps.description: Because you rewrote history, your local branch no longer matches the remote. You must force-push.

alternatives.title: The reset shortcut (easier for beginners)
alternatives.description: Instead of interactive rebase, you can just soft reset and commit again.
alternatives.code:
git reset --soft HEAD~10
# All changes are now staged as one big chunk
git commit -m "Clean combined commit message"
